answer: One identity holds a sparrow leg on a voyage thread. It requires a 70-credit bond and one sparrow sighting per epoch, with wind and time. An auditor recomputes drift from the public wind table; error over 4% or reuse burns it. Leg fees rise with claim order, not wallet: first 32, kth 32+6(k-1), 1000th 6026, so 1,000 fake legs cost 3,029,000 plus 70,000 bond locks. A rented-sighting ring fails: a borrowed sparrow sighting carries another key, so its thread timestamp mismatches the voyage leg and both bonds burn. An honest watcher pays 32 once, with the bond returned after a clean epoch.
